This fun project by Jeff Halter (introduced by Daring Fireball) lets users run original 68k After Dark screensaver modules on modern Macs. Details below.

「喺現代 macOS 上運行經典 After Dark 螢幕保護程式」

Depending on how long ago you started using or became interested in Macs, you probably remember After Dark—a screensaver suite that was practically a must-have for Macintosh computers in the 1990s. At the very least, you might recall that classic 「flying toast」 screensaver.

Over the years, running these classic screensavers typically required vintage hardware or a classic Mac OS emulator, and the latter was often a hassle. However, a new project called Afterglow makes the process of running them on modern Macs much simpler.

As mentioned by John Gruber on Daring Fireball, this project comes from Jeff Halter, who previously created Lunacy—a natively Swift-written application that lets users play the classic game Lunatic Fringe from More After Dark on modern Macs.

Afterglow runs original After Dark modules through an emulator specifically designed for these modules, without needing a complete classic Mac OS environment. Notably, Afterglow also includes a modern macOS screensaver module, allowing users to set any imported After Dark module as their Mac's screensaver.

Here's Halter's sharing on the creative motivation behind this project:

In the 90s, Berkeley Systems' After Dark screensaver brought flying toast, swimming goldfish, and starry night skies to Macintosh screens everywhere. Beyond its practical function of preventing image burn-in on CRT displays, it also brought plenty of fun—the animations were sometimes funny, sometimes surreal, sometimes beautiful—occasionally even a bit disturbing. These are works of art worth preserving.

The project's official website notes that Afterglow itself does not come bundled with After Dark modules, but provides tutorials on how to import these modules.

Halter also mentioned that Afterglow includes various features such as module controls, full-screen mode, random playback, multi-module support, 3D cover flow, CRT shader, resource viewer, and DrawMorph editor.
